questions.q: A uniform circular disc of radius ' R ' and mass ' M ' is rotating about an axis perpendicular to its plane and passing through its centre. A small circular part of radius $\mathrm{R} / 2$ is removed from the original disc as shown in the figure. Find the moment of inertia of the remaining part of the original disc about the axis as given above.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & I_{\text {complete }}=\frac{M R^2}{2} \\ & \begin{aligned} I_{\text {removed }} & =\left(\frac{M}{4}\right)\left(\frac{R}{2}\right)^2 \frac{1}{2}+\left(\frac{M}{4}\right)\left(\frac{R}{2}\right)^2 \\ & =\frac{3 M R^2}{32} \\ I=\frac{M R^2}{2} & -\frac{3 M R^2}{32}=\frac{13}{32} M R^2\end{aligned}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The magnitude of torque on a particle of mass $1 \mathrm{~kg}$ is 2.5 Nm about the origin. If the force acting on it is $1 \mathrm{~N},$ and the distance of the particle from the origin is $5 \mathrm{~m},$ the angle between the force and the position vector is (in radians):
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Torque about the origin $=\vec{\tau}=\overrightarrow{\mathrm{r}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{F}}=r F \sin \theta \Rightarrow 2.5=1 \times 5 \sin \theta\sin \theta=0.5=\frac{1}{2}\Rightarrow \theta=\frac{\pi}{6}$

questions.q: A body A of mass $m$ is moving in a circular orbit of radius $R$ about a planet. Another body B of mass $\dfrac{m}{2}$ collides with A with a velocity which is half  \left(\dfrac{\overset{→}{v}}{2}\right)$ the instantaneous velocity $\overset{→}{v}$ of A. The collision is completely inelastic. Then, the combined body:$
options: continues to move in a circular orbit
Escapes from the Planet's Gravitational field
Falls vertically downwards towards the planet
starts moving in an elliptical orbit around the planet
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Conserving momentum
$\dfrac{m}{2}\dfrac{v}{2} + mv = \left(m + \dfrac{m}{2}\right){v}_{f}$
${v}_{f} = \dfrac{2mV}{4 \times \dfrac{3m}{2}} = \dfrac{5V}{6}$
${v}_{f} < {v}_{orb} \left(=v\right) thus the combined mass will go on to an elliptical path$

questions.q: The solid cylinder of length $80$ cm and mass $M$ has a radius of $20cm .$ Calculate the density of the material used if the moment of inertia of the cylinder about an axis $CD$ parallel to $AB$ as shown in figure is $2 . 7kgm^{2}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$I = \dfrac{Mr^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{ML^{2}}{4} = \dfrac{ \left($ρ\pir^{2}L\right)r^{2}}{2} + \left(ρ\pir^{2}L\right)\dfrac{L2}{4}$

$= ρ\pir^{2}L\left(\dfrac{r2}{2} + \dfrac{L2}{4}\right)$

$⇒ ρ = \dfrac{I}{\pir^{2}L\left(\dfrac{r2}{2} + \dfrac{L2}{4}\right)}$

On putting the values, we get~$ρ = 1 . 49 \times {10}^{2}kgm^{- 3}$.

$

questions.q:
A solid cylinder of mass $m$ is wrapped with an inextensible light string and, is placed on a rough inclined plane as shown in the figure. The frictional force acting between the cylinder and the inclined plane is:

[The coefficient of static friction, ${μ}_{s}$,~is $0 . 4$& ]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let's take solid cylinder is in equilibrium

$T + f = mgsin60$

$TR - fR = 0$

Solving we get

$T = {f}_{req} = \dfrac{mgsin\theta}{2}$

But limiting friction $<$ required friction

$\mumgcos60 ° < \dfrac{mg sin60 °}{2}$

$∴$ Hence cylinder will not remain in equilibrium

Hence $f =$ kinetic

$= {μ}_{k}N$

$= {μ}_{k}mgcos60 °$

$= \dfrac{mg}{5}$

questions.q: A uniform rod of length $l$ is being rotated in a horizontal plane with a constant angular speed about an axis passing through one of its ends. If the tension generated in the rod due to rotation is $T ( x )$ at a distance $x$ from the axis, then which of the following graphs depicts it most closely?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The mass of the rod at a distance& $x$~from the axis is~$dm = \dfrac{M}{L} . dx$
$T = ( dm ) {\omega}^{2}x$

Integrating~the above equation from~$x$~to~$L$
$= {∫}_x^{L}\dfrac{M}{L}{\omega}^{2}xdx$
$= \dfrac{M}{L}{\omega}^{2}{ \left[\dfrac{x^{2}}{2}\right]}_x^{L}$
$\dfrac{M}{2L}{\omega}^{2}\left[$L^{2} - x^{2}\right]$
The above equation \text{ and } depicts the relation \text{ and } between tension and length of rod as downward opening parabola.

$

questions.q: A thin smooth rod of length $L$ and mass $M$ is rotating freely with angular speed ${\omega}_{0}$ about an axis perpendicular to the rod and passing through center. Two beads of mass $m$ and negligible size are at the center of the rod initially. The beads of mass $m$ and negligible size are at the center of the rod initially. The beads are free to slide along the rod. The angular speed of the system, when the beads reach the opposite ends of the rod, will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From conservation of angular momentum.
$\dfrac{ML^{2}}{12}{\omega}_{0} = \left[\dfrac{ML^{2}}{12} + m{\left(\dfrac{L}{2}\right)}^{2} + m{\left(\dfrac{L}{2}\right)}^{2}\right]\omega'$
$\dfrac{ML^{2}}{12}{\omega}_{0} = \left(\dfrac{ML^{2}}{12} + \dfrac{mL^{2}}{2}\right)\omega'$
$\omega' = \dfrac{M{\omega}_{0}}{M + 6m}$

questions.q: A solid sphere and solid cylinder of identical radii approach an incline with the same linear velocity (see figure). Both roll without slipping all throughout. The two climb maximum heights ${h}_{sph}$ and ${h}_{cyl}$ on the inline. The ratio $\dfrac{{h}_{sph}}{{h}_{cyl}}$ is given by:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From conservation of mechanical energy,
For solid sphere: $\dfrac{1}{2}{m}_{sph}V^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}{I}_{sph}{\omega}^{2} = {m}_{sph}g{h}_{sph}$
$\dfrac{V^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{V^{2}}{5} = g{h}_{sph}$
$\dfrac{7V^{2}}{10} = g{h}_{sph}$ …(i)
For cylinder: $\dfrac{1}{2}{m}_{cyl}V^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}{I}_{cyl}{\omega}^{2} = {m}_{cyl}g{h}_{cyl}$
$\dfrac{V^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{V^{2}}{4} = g{h}_{cyl}$
$\dfrac{3V^{2}}{4} = g{h}_{cyl}$ …(ii)
From (i) and (ii) $\dfrac{{h}_{sph}}{{h}_{cyl}} = \dfrac{14}{15}$

questions.q: A wheel is rotating freely with an angular speed $\omega$ on a shaft. The moment of inertia of the wheel is $I$ and the moment of inertia of the shaft is negligible. Another wheel of moment of inertia $3I$ initially at rest is suddenly coupled to the same shaft. The resultant fractional loss in the kinetic energy of the system is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From angular momentum conservation
$I\omega + 0 = I{ω}_{C} + 3I{ω}_{C}$
$\omegac = \dfrac{ω}{4}$

Loss of kinetic energy~$= \dfrac{1}{2}I{ω}^{2} - \dfrac{1}{2} ( I + 3I ) \left(\dfrac{ω}{4}\right)2$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}I{ω}^{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}I\dfrac{\omega2}{4}$

$= \dfrac{3}{8}I{ω}^{2}$

Fractional loss~$= \dfrac{3}{4}$

questions.q: A person of mass $M$ is sitting on a swing of length $L$ and swinging with and an angular amplitude ${\theta}_{0} .$ If the person stands up when the swing passes through its lowest point, the work done by him, assuming that his centre of mass moves by a distance $l\left(l < < L\right),$ is close to:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From angular momentum conservation
M{V}_{0}L = MV ( L - l )
V = {V}_{0} \left(\dfrac{L}{L - l}\right)$

Now
$W = Mgl + \dfrac{1}{2}M \left[{V0}^{2} $\$left(\dfrac{L}{L - l}\right)2 - {V0}^{2}\right]$
Since $l ≪ L$
W = Mgl + $\d$dfrac{1}{2}M\left[{V0}^{2}\left($1 - \dfrac{l}{L}\right)-2 - {V0}^{2}\right]
= Mgl + \dfrac{1}{2}M \left[{V0}^{2} \left(1 + 2\dfrac{l}{L}\right) - {V0}^{2}\right]
= Mgl + M \left[{V0}^{2} \left(\dfrac{l}{L}\right)\right]$

From SHM
${V}_{0} = \omegaA = \sqrt{\dfrac{g}{L}} \timesL{θ}_{0} = \sqrt{gL}{θ}_{0}$
Using this
W = Mgl + $M \left[gL \times {\theta0}^{2} \times \left(\dfrac{l}{L}\right)\right]
W = Mgl\left[1 + {\theta0}^{2}\right]
$

questions.q: A thin circular ring of mass $M$ and radius $r$ is rotating about its axis with an angular speed $\omega .$~Two particles having mass $m$ each are now attached at diametrically opposite points. The angular speed of the ring will become:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Using conservation of angular momentum
$⇒ \left(Mr^{2}\right)\omega = \left(Mr^{2} + 2mr^{2}\right){ω}^{'}$

$⇒ {ω}^{'} = \dfrac{M\omega}{M + 2m}$.

questions.q: ${I}_{CM}$ is moment of inertia of a circular disc about an axis (CM) passing through its center and perpendicular to the plane of disc. ${I}_{AB}$ is its moment of inertia about an axis AB~perpendicular to plane and parallel to axis CM~at a distance $\dfrac{2}{3}R$ from center,~where R~is the radius of the disc. The ratio of ${I}_{AB}$ and ${I}_{CM}$ is $x: 9$. The value of $x$& is ______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
We have, ${I}_{CM} = \dfrac{1}{2}MR^{2}$

Since $AB$ is parallel to diameter and at a distance of~$\dfrac{2}{3}R$~from it, using parallel axis theorem,

${I}_{AB} = \dfrac{mR^{2}}{2} + m\left(\dfrac{2R}{3}\right)2 = \dfrac{17}{18}mR^{2}$

Thus, the ratio is~

$∴ \dfrac{IAB}{ICM} = \dfrac{\dfrac{17}{18}MR^{2}}{\dfrac{1}{2}MR^{2}} = \dfrac{17}{9}$

Thus,~$x = 17$

questions.q: The position vector of $1$ kg object is $\overset{→}{r} = \left(3\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j}\right)m$ and its velocity $\overset{→}{v} = \left(3\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)ms^{- 1}$. The magnitude of its angular momentum is $\sqrt{x}Nms$,~where $x$ is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Angular momentum of a particle is given by,

$\overset{→}{L} = \overset{→}{r} \times \overset{→}{P} = \overset{→}{r} \times m\overset{→}{v}$~also~$m = 1kg$.

$⇒ \overset{→}{L} = \left(3\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j}\right) \times \left(3\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right) = \left(9\overset{^}{k} - 3\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{i}\right)Nms$

The magnitude of the angular momentum will be,

$⇒ \left|\overset{→}{L}\right| = \sqrt{{9}^{2} + {3}^{2} + {1}^{2}} = \sqrt{91}Nms$

Therefore, the value of~$x = 91$.

questions.q: A solid sphere and a hollow cylinder roll up without slipping on same inclined plane with same initial speed $v$. The sphere and the cylinder reaches upto maximum heights $h_1$ and $h_2$, respectively, above the initial level. The ratio $h_1: h_2$ is $\frac{n}{10}$. The value of $n$ is______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Gain in P.E. = Loss in K.E.
$\mathrm{mgh}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}^2\left(1+\frac{\mathrm{K}^2}{\mathrm{R}^2}\right)\mathrm{h} \propto 1+\frac{\mathrm{K}^2}{\mathrm{R}^2}\frac{\mathrm{h}_1}{\mathrm{~h}_2}=\frac{1+\frac{2}{5}}{1+1}=\frac{7}{5 \times 2}=\frac{7}{10}\mathrm{n}=7$
